articles.title: The Curious Case of 'Warsh': Tracing an American Dialect's Scotch-Irish Roots
articles.summary: Why do some Americans say "warsh" for "wash"? Linguists point to Scotch-Irish immigration in the 18th century. These rhotic speakers—meaning they pronounce "r" strongly—spread the dialect across Appalachia and beyond. Though fading, you can still hear it from older generations in regions from Baltimore to Washington state.

articles.title: Trump's Iran Deal Hopes Collide with Renewed Bombing Threats
articles.summary: Trump suspended "Project Freedom" to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz, claiming progress toward a 14-point peace deal with Iran. But within hours, he threatened "much higher" bombing if no deal is signed. Experts warn negotiations are fragile, and Iran calls the plan a U.S. wish list.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV to Inaugurate Sagrada Familia's Tower and Visit Migrant Hub in Spain
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV's June trip to Spain will blend grandeur and compassion. He'll inaugurate the 172.5-meter Tower of Jesus Christ at Barcelona's Sagrada Familia, marking 100 years since Antoni Gaudí's death. Then he heads to the Canary Islands to meet migrants at a reception center, following in Pope Francis's footsteps.
